comparator.name: Public Administration
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme pages establish a coherent 180-EC Public Administration pathway: ten compulsory 6-EC courses in year 1; eight compulsory 6-EC courses and two 6-EC restricted electives in year 2; and 18 EC of compulsory advanced study, 30 EC of genuine free choice and a 12-EC bachelor thesis in year 3. The two restricted electives are instantiated as the first two options in the published list—Security in the Netherlands: Policy and Organisation and Challenges in Policy Advising—as a neutral choice independent of UCR fit. The programme has no formal named route, so no route is selected.

alternatives.label: Public policy, governance & institutions
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible public-administration programme combining public policy and institutions with law, politics, economics, sociology, organisational behaviour, European governance and mixed research methods.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is centred on public policy and governance but combines political, legal, economic, sociological, organisational and methodological study, so the label names that substantive combination.
progression: Political, sociological, economic, research and legal foundations precede advanced public economics, EU law and politics, organisational psychology, communication and econometrics. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

develops negotiation, strategic interaction and decision-making for policy processes
examines motivation, groups, organisational culture and structures in public and other organisations
examines leadership, inclusion and diversity within organisations

alternatives.label: Climate policy & sustainability governance
alternatives.concept: A governance programme organised around climate change and sustainability transitions, combining environmental science and sustainability analysis with institutions, law, economics, public participation, communication and research.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum places climate science, sustainability systems and environmental applications inside a substantial governance, law, economics and research framework.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad public-administration programme, this route replaces twelve courses in general administration, security, organisations and methods with a sequenced climate, sustainability, environmental-science, environmental-justice and climate-communication strand.
progression: Sustainability, climate, politics and research foundations precede advanced sustainability governance, environmental science, EU governance and applied sustainability research. Sustainability Essentials I precedes Sustainability Essentials II and Earth's Resources. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Public organisations, leadership & digital governance
alternatives.concept: A public-governance programme centred on how organisations function, lead change and respond to digital transformation, combining political and legal institutions with strategy, leadership, organisational psychology, data, communication and applied research.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum retains public institutions, law and economics while concentrating its distinctive courses on organisations, leadership, strategy, digital transformation, data and communication.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest programme, this route replaces seven courses in broad policy, security, macroeconomics and social theory with business foundations, strategy, digital governance, international governance, leadership communication and applied organisational research; it differs from the climate route by sixteen courses.
progression: Politics, business, data, research, sociology, communication and law foundations precede advanced strategy, organisational leadership, international governance, EU politics, market research and econometrics. Business Foundations and Research Methods & Statistics precede every course that formally requires them, and every course is offered in its assigned term.

candidates.label: Public organisations, leadership and digital governance

selection.assessment: The broad closest match covers the programme's institutional, policy, legal, economic, organisational and methodological core. Climate policy supports a coherent sustainability-governance route, while the functioning of public organisations supports a distinct leadership and digital-governance route. The housing-and-poverty cluster is assessed separately but rejected because the current UCR catalogue cannot sustain a credible 24-course housing and social-policy programme without replacing its subject with general sociology, economics or governance. The included pairs differ by twelve, seven and sixteen courses respectively, so all exceed the pairwise 30-EC floor. The maximum of three alternatives is reached.

blocks: Both examine political institutions, government and comparative political systems.
Both analyse societal problems and the institutions and inequalities that shape them.
Both examine public institutions and constitutional arrangements; UCR does so comparatively.
Both address decision-making among actors with competing interests; UCR emphasises negotiation and strategic interaction.
Both examine the relationship between law, public authority and society.
Both address security and the political organisation of responses to conflict and threat.
Both examine EU institutions, decision-making and multilevel governance.
Both examine governance and institutions across borders; UCR approaches this through international organisational governance.
UCR distributes public-administration foundations across politics, law, sociology, economics and organisations rather than offering one dedicated core course.
UCR has no dedicated public-policy integration simulation in the scheduled curricula.
UCR addresses governance and organisational change but has no dedicated policy-implementation course in the current catalogue.
Both analyse changing relations between institutions, society and citizens.
Both examine how organisations function and are managed; UCR uses organisational psychology and leadership.
Both develop normative analysis of good governance, responsibility and contested public choices.
Both develop evidence-based communication and persuasion for advising and public decision-making.
UCR addresses ethics and public values through several courses, but no second scheduled course directly reproduces this dedicated component.
The UCR curricula include applied research and problem solving but no dedicated short public-administration hackathon.
Both introduce research design and quantitative evidence for public or organisational questions.
Both develop qualitative research design, data collection and interpretation.
Both examine economic analysis of public policy, including market failure and government intervention.
Both provide advanced quantitative analysis for policy-relevant evidence; UCR focuses on econometrics.
Both analyse how digital technologies reshape organisations, governance and public choices.
Radboud requires a separate 12-EC bachelor thesis. UCR's standardized optional independent-research element is shown alongside this component.
Both develop academic source use, argument, communication, collaboration and reflective professional skills.
This is genuine free-choice space. UCR flexibility is distributed across the complete 180-EC curriculum, so no single scheduled course is asserted as its equivalent.

notes.text: Radboud's programme provides a dedicated sequence in public-administration theory, policy formation and implementation, public organisations, policy methods, European and comparative administration, digital government and a bachelor thesis. UCR can combine politics, law, economics, sociology, organisations, research and thematic governance into coherent programmes, but it does not reproduce the full specialist public-administration sequence course by course.
